For the future memory of the matter.

units.la: Revelabo pudenda tua in faciem tuam: & osten-
units.tr: I will uncover your nakedness to your face,

units.la: dam in gentibus nuditatem tuam, & regnis
units.tr: and I will show the nations your nudity, and the kingdoms
your shame.

units.la: BENEDICTIONES S. D. N. PAPÆ SIXTI V. IN REGEM NAVARRVM ET PRINCIPEM CONDAEVM.
units.tr: BLESSINGS (BENEDICTIONES) OF OUR MOST HOLY LORD POPE SIXTUS V AGAINST THE KING OF NAVARRE AND THE PRINCE OF CONDÉ.
Page 1.

units.la: Exercemus arma militiæ nostræ contra duos iræ filios Henricū Borbonium, QVONDAM Nauarræ regem, & Henricum item Borbonium OLIM Principem Condensem. Ille hæreses ab ineunte adolescentia secutus pertinax earum patrocinium exercuit.
units.tr: We wage the arms of our warfare against two sons of wrath: Henry of Bourbon, formerly King of Navarre, and likewise Henry of Bourbon, once Prince of Condé. The former, following heresies from his early youth, pertinaciously practised their defence.
Page 2.

units.la: Idem revolutus in cœno, caput, dux, & propugnator hæreticorum & perduellium, arma contra regem suum Christianissimum aduersus i[?]psum & reliquos catholicos sumpsit: ciues regni ad suam capescendam impietatem verberibus coegit: con-ciliabula hæreticorum habenda cu-rauit.
units.tr: The same man, having wallowed in the mire, as head, leader and champion of heretics and traitors, took up arms against his Most Christian King, against himself and the other Catholics. He compelled the citizens of the realm, with blows, to embrace his impiety, and he saw to it that conventicles of heretics were held.
Page 3.

units.la: Princeps Condæus utroque parente hæretico genitus, patris, & matris secutus hæreses, viam patris sui impiissimi catholicæ ecclesiæ persecu-toris ingressus, bellorum civilium & seditionum auctorem se præbuit, omne feritatis & sævitiæ genus exercuit: proles detestabilis ac degener familia Borboniorum.
units.tr: The Prince of Condé, born of two heretical parents, followed the heresies of his father and mother. Entering upon the way of his most impious father, a persecutor of the Catholic Church, he showed himself the author of civil wars and seditions, and practised every kind of savagery and cruelty. He is a detestable offspring, and a degenerate member of the Bourbon family.
Page ibid.

units.la: Pronunciamus illos esse hæreticos, in hæreses relapsos, impœnitentes, hæreticorum duces & fautores, & læsæ maiestatis diuinæ reos, & fidei Christiana hostes, priuatos illū Nauar-ra regno, hūc, & utrúque, eorúmque posteros omnibus principatibus, du-catibus, dominiis, & feudis, hono-ribus & officiis regiis: fuisse & esse inhabiles & incapaces ad illa reti-nenda.
units.tr: We declare that they are heretics, relapsed into heresy, impenitent, leaders and supporters of heretics, guilty of divine treason, and enemies of the Christian faith; that he has been deprived of the kingdom of Navarre, and that this man and both of them, with their descendants, are and have been unfit and incapable of retaining all principalities, duchies, dominions and fiefs, and royal honours and offices.
Page 4.

units.la: Ac pariter priuatos, incapaces, & inhabiles ad succedendum in ducati-bus, principatibus, ac regnis, & spe-cialiter in regno Francia: & ex-abundanti nos illos illorúmque poste-ros priuamus in perpetuum & inha-bilitamus ad successionem in ducati-bus, principatibus, dominijs, & re-gnis, & signanter in Francia regno.
units.tr: And likewise we deprive them, and their descendants, as incapable and unfit to succeed to duchies, principalities and kingdoms, and especially to the kingdom of France; and, out of abundance of power, we deprive them and their descendants forever, and render them unfit for succession to duchies, principalities, dominions and kingdoms, and especially to the kingdom of France.
Page ibid.

units.la: Proceres, feudatarios, vasallos, & cateros omnes qui illis quomodocunque iurauerint, ab eiusmodi iu-rameto & fidelitatis & obsequij de-bito absoluimus & liberamus: & in-terdicimus ne illis audeant obedire,
units.tr: We absolve and release from the oath and from the debt of fidelity and obedience all nobles, feudatories, vassals and all others who have sworn allegiance to them in any way, and we forbid them to dare to obey them.
Page ibid.

units.la: Monemus & hortamur Fran-corum Regem Christianissimum ut ad executionem nostræ sententiæ incumbat. Datum Romæ, 5. Id. Sept. anno 1585.
units.tr: We admonish and exhort the Most Christian King of the French to apply himself to the execution of our sentence. Given at Rome, on the fifth day before the Ides of September, in the year 1585.
Response from Psalm 109.

units.la: Domine, maledicent illi & tu benedices: qui insurgent in me confundentur,seruus autem tuus lætabitur.
units.tr: Let them curse, Lord, but you will bless; let those who rise up against me be confounded, but your servant will rejoice.

units.la: BRVTVM FVLMEN PAPÆ SIXTI V. ADVERSVS HENRICVM SERENISSIMVM Regem Nauarræ, & illustriss. Henricum Borbonium, Principem Condæum.
units.tr: THE BRUTE THUNDERBOLT OF POPE SIXTUS V AGAINST HENRY, MOST SERENE KING OF NAVARRE, AND THE MOST ILLUSTRIOUS HENRY OF BOURBON, PRINCE OF CONDÉ.

units.la: Vnà cum protestatione & declaratione multiplicis nullitatis.
units.tr: Together with a protest and declaration of manifold nullity.

units.la: VOD nuper à Papa Sixto quinto Franciscano pronuntiata Declaratio est, paulóque póst edita & promulgata, vt Henricus Sereniss. Rex Nauarræ, itémque Henricus Borbonius Illustrissimus Princeps Condæus primùm tanquam hæretici notorij ex communione Christianorum arcerentur, tum vt imperiis, honoribus, dignitatibus omnibus, ac potissimùm spe legitimæ successionis regni Galliæ abdicarentur: deinde vt eorum clientes ac vassalli fidelitatis iuramento, quo illis obstricti sunt, soluerentur: postremò vt à potentissimo Rege Galliæ vi, ferro, armis, & castris oppugnarentur: DE EA RE Supradicti Serenissimi & Illustrissimi Principes ita protestati sunt: bona Catholicorum omnium pace, saluáque religionis vtriusque concordia, quam iidem Principes magnopere in Gallia conseruari cupiunt, proscriptionem, siue DECLARATIONEM illam Papæ monachi Franciscani, contra iura omnia divina & humana pronuntiatam, editam, ac promulgatà fuisse: ob eámque caussam ipso iure nullam, ac pro nulla habendam esse: totámque illam furibundam execratione aliud nihil esse, nisi brutum Papatus R. fulmen, cuius inanes, vani ac ventosi sunt impetus: ídque quatuor præcipuè de caussis: nempe, propter temerarij iudicis incompetètiam, allegationis falsitatè, ordinis iudicialis defectum, & conceptæ formulæ stultitiam: de quibus eo, quo propositæ sunt, ordine, deinceps differemus.
units.tr: The Declaration recently pronounced by Pope Sixtus V, a Franciscan, and soon afterwards published and promulgated, has these aims: first, that Henry, the most serene King of Navarre, and likewise Henry of Bourbon, the most illustrious Prince of Condé, be cut off from the communion of Christians as notorious heretics; then, that they be stripped of command, honours, all dignities, and above all of their hope of lawful succession to the kingdom of France; next, that their clients and vassals be released from the oath of fidelity by which they are bound to them; and finally, that they be attacked by force, steel, arms and camps by the most powerful King of France. CONCERNING THIS MATTER the aforesaid most serene and illustrious Princes have protested as follows: that, with the good peace of all Catholics and the preservation of concord in both religions, which these same Princes earnestly desire to be kept in France, that proscription, or DECLARATION, of the Franciscan monk Pope, pronounced and published against all divine and human law, is void in law and must be held as nothing; and for this reason that whole furious curse is nothing but the brute thunderbolt of the Papacy, whose assaults are empty, vain and windy. And this rests chiefly on four grounds: namely, the incompetence of the rash judge, the falsity of the allegation, the defect of judicial procedure, and the folly of the form of words used. We shall deal with these in the order in which they have been set out.
On the incompetence of the judge.

units.la: PRima igitur NVLLITATIS caussa est temerarij iudicis incompetentia, quæ ex eo perspicitur, quòd Papatus Romanus, qui sibi hoc in tantos principes iudicium sumpsit, iam pridem a maxima Christianitatis parte, nempe Anglia, Scotia, Dania, Suecia, maxima Germaniæ, itémque maxima Heluetiæ parte septem grauissimorum criminum nomine damnatus est:nimirum impietatis, tyrannidis in ecclesia occupatæ, corruptæ religionis, sacrilegij, maiestatis, perduellionis, & falsi.Certum est autem, etiam si nondum tantorum criminum damnatus fuisset, sed reus duntaxat factus, tamen, non dico iudicem ei esse non licere, sed ne infimum quidem ac tenuissimum hominem, ullius culpæ aut delicti accusare, priusquam illis se omnibus criminibus idoneè purgasset: tantum abest, ut in hoc rerum statu tantos & tam illustres ac potentes Principes tanti sceleris, præsertim inauditos, & causa indicta, condemnare possit.
units.tr: The first cause of nullity, then, is the incompetence of the rash judge, which is evident from this: the Roman Papacy, which has claimed for itself this judgment over such great princes, has for some time now been condemned by the greatest part of Christendom, namely England, Scotland, Denmark, Sweden, most of Germany, and likewise most of Helvetia, on seven most grave charges: impiety, tyranny exercised over the Church, corruption of religion, sacrilege, treason (maiestas), perduellion, and forgery. It is certain, moreover, that even if it had not yet been condemned for such great crimes, but had merely been made a defendant, it would not be lawful for it to act as judge, not only over princes but even over the lowest and most humble man, in accusing him of any fault or crime, until it had properly cleared itself of all those charges. So far is it from being able, in the present state of affairs, to condemn such great, illustrious and powerful princes of so great a crime, especially one so unheard of, and without the case having been heard.

units.la: l.neganda, 19.C. de his qui accuf. non possunt.l.si qui reus[?] 8.D.de public.judi. quod idem ab ipsis Canonistis traditur. 4.quaest.1.c.1.25.q.1.c.omnes 24.quaest.1.c.aut,& duobus capp.seqq. Quinetiam illud accedit, quòd cùm in hac supradictorum principum causa de re & statu ipsius Papatus potissimum agatur, nulla nec civilis,nec naturalis ratio patitur,eum rei suæ judicem sedere, sibique de re propria jus dicere. l.qui iurisdictioni,D.de iurisd.l.1.C.ne quis in sua causa iud.l.Julianus,17.de judic. Quòd si Papa judex in hac causa non est idoneus, sed incompetens & incon-gruus, quemadmodum ex iis quæ posterius dicen-tur dilucidè constabit: sequitur, ut sententia ab eo pronuntiata ipso jure nulla sit, & per se, ac sine appellatione vlla concidat. l.1.& pass.C.si non comper. iud.l.6.§.quod si quis,D.de iniust.rupt.test. Plurimum autem momenti habiturum esse apud regni Gallici magistratus, atque ordines, ac præsertim apud eiusdem regni Parlamenta supradictæ maximæ Christianitatis partis judicium atque auctoritatem, dubitare non possumus: cùm omnium gentium hoc jus esse constet, ut in deliberationibus, præsertim arduis & grauibus, semper ex maioris partis sententia judicetur. l.item si unus,17.§.vlt.& l.seq.D.de recep.arbit. præsertim ubi maior pars non tantùm ex personarum numero, verùm etiam ex universi ordinis modo & quantitate censetur: veluti cùm e tribus judicum partibus duæ discef-sionem faciunt: puta octo e duodecim. l.3.de decret. ab ord.fac.l.3.& l.4. D.quod cuiusque universitatis. l.nominationum,46.C.de decurio. l.quod maior.19.D.ad municipal. Angliam autem, Scotiam, Daniam, Sue-tiam, maximam Heluetiæ & Germaniæ superioris & inferioris partem facile duas Christianitatis partes è tribus obtinere,ac proinde magnum apud ordines & Parlamenta Galliæ pondus atque auctoritatem habituras,pro singulari nostro de prudentia illorum iudicio ambigere nec possumus, nec debemus. Quin ne illud quidem praetermit-tendum videtur, Papam non tantum à maxima Europæ parte pro incongruo & incompetente iudice reiectum esse, verum etiam ab iis Ecclesiis & nationibus, quæ in Africa, Ægypto, Syria, Oriente, Asia, & Græcia nomen suum inter Christianas Ecclesias profitentur.
units.tr: l.neganda, 19.C. de his qui accuf. non possunt.l.si qui reus[?] 8.D.de public.judi. The same is taught by the Canonists themselves: 4.quaest.1.c.1.25.q.1.c.omnes 24.quaest.1.c.aut,& duobus capp.seqq. Moreover, this is added: since in this case of the aforesaid princes the matter concerns chiefly the affair and the state of the Papacy itself, no civil or natural reason permits that it should sit as judge in its own affair and pronounce law in its own cause. l.qui iurisdictioni,D.de iurisd.l.1.C.ne quis in sua causa iud.l.Julianus,17.de judic. But if the Pope is not a suitable judge in this cause, but incompetent and unfit, as will become clear from what is said below, it follows that the sentence pronounced by him is null in law, and falls of itself, without any appeal. l.1.& pass.C.si non comper. iud.l.6.§.quod si quis,D.de iniust.rupt.test. Moreover, we cannot doubt that the judgment and authority of the aforesaid greatest part of Christendom will carry great weight with the magistrates and orders of the kingdom of France, and especially with the Parlements of that kingdom; since it is established that this is the law of all nations, that in deliberations, especially difficult and weighty ones, judgment is always given by the opinion of the greater part. l.item si unus,17.§.vlt.& l.seq.D.de recep.arbit. This holds especially where the greater part is reckoned not only by the number of persons but also by the manner and the quantity of the whole body; as when two of three parts of judges make a separation, for instance eight out of twelve. l.3.de decret. ab ord.fac.l.3.& l.4. D.quod cuiusque universitatis. l.nominationum,46.C.de decurio. l.quod maior.19.D.ad municipal. That England, Scotland, Denmark, Sweden, the greater part of Helvetia and of Upper and Lower Germany together hold easily two parts of Christendom out of three, and therefore will have great weight and authority with the orders and Parlements of France, we neither can nor ought to doubt, given our singular confidence in their prudence and judgment. Nor does it seem that this should be passed over: the Pope has been rejected as an unfitting and incompetent judge not only by the greatest part of Europe, but also by those churches and nations which in Africa, Egypt, Syria, the East, Asia and Greece profess their name among the Christian churches.

units.la: Crimen impietatis multiplex, ac primum de arrogata divinitate.
units.tr: The crime of impiety, first concerning the arrogated divinity.

units.la: PRImum igitur crimen, cuius à maxima Europæ parte Papatus Romanus conuictus & condemnatus est, dicimus esse Impietatem, eámque triplicem: primùm quia Papa sibi Diuinitatem asciscit: deinde quia religionem Christianam illudit ac deridet: postremò quia falsas & commentitias religiones in Ecclesiam induxit. Primæ im-pietatis testimonia hæc sunt: Papa DEVM se appellari, & gaudet, & gloriatur. dist. 96. c. satis: ubi scriptum ita est: Satis ostenditur à seculari potestate nec ligari prorsus, nec solui posse Pontificem, quem constat à pio Principe Constantino DEVM appellatum: cum nec Deum posse ab hominibus iudicari manifestum sit. Quem locum Augustinus Steuchus insignis Papæ Romani parasitaster eiusdemque Bibliothecarius in lib. de donat. Constant. pag. 141. laudans, & commemorans, ita subiungit: Audis summum Pontificem à Constantino DEVM appellatum,& habitu pro DEO? Hoc videlicet factu est, cum eū præclaro illo edicto decoram it, ADORAVIT uti DEVM,uti Christi & Petri successorem: diuinos honores ei, quoad eius potuit, contulit, velut uiuam Christi imaginem veneratus est. Haec Steuchus in supradicto libro, edito Lugduni anno 1547. Ex eodem impietatis genere illud est glossae in praefat. Clement. Papa nec Deus est, nec homo, sed neuter est inter utrumque. unde versus apud Canonistas visitatus,
units.tr: FIrst, then, the crime for which the Roman Papacy has been convicted and condemned by the greater part of Europe, we say is impiety, and that a threefold one: first, because the Pope assumes divinity for himself; second, because he mocks and derides the Christian religion; and lastly, because he has introduced false and fabricated religions into the Church. The testimonies to the first impiety are these: the Pope is glad and boasts that he is called God. Dist. 96, c. satis: where it is written thus: It is shown sufficiently that the Pontiff, whom it is agreed was called God by the pious Emperor Constantine, can be neither bound nor loosed by secular power, since it is plain that God cannot be judged by men. Augustinus Steuchus, the distinguished parasite of the Roman Pope and his librarian, quotes and cites this passage in his book on the Donation of Constantine, p. 141, and adds the following: Do you hear that the supreme Pontiff was called God by Constantine and held to be God? Clearly this happened when, with that famous edict, he adorned him, worshipped him as God, as the successor of Christ and Peter; he bestowed divine honours on him, as far as he could, and venerated him as a living image of Christ. Thus Steuchus in the book cited above, published at Lyons in 1547. Of the same kind of impiety is the gloss on the preface to the Clementines: The Pope is neither God nor man, but is something between the two. Hence the verse commonly cited among the canonists:

units.la: Papa stupor mundi, solus qui maxime rerum,Nec Deus es, nec homo, sed neuter es inter utrumque.
units.tr:
Pope, wonder of the world, who alone are greatest of all things,
Thou art neither God nor man, but something between the two.

units.la: itemque illud alterum in c. fundamenta, de elect. in 6. vbi, cum in textu scriptum esset, Papam nulli homini subesse, ita subiungit, Et in hac parte Papa non est homo, sed Dei vicarius. Sequitur altera blasphemia, ex libro Ceremon. Pontifical. 1. tit. 7.
units.tr: and likewise that other passage in c. fundamenta, de elect. in 6, where, though the text says the Pope is subject to no man, the gloss adds: And in this respect the Pope is not a man, but the vicar of God. There follows another blasphemy, from the book of Pontifical Ceremonies, 1, tit. 7.

units.la: Papa, inquit, in nocte natiuitatis Domini benedicit ensem, quem postea donat alicui principi, in signum infinitae potentiae Pontifici collatae: iuxta illud, Data est mihi potestas in coelo & in terra. Item, Dominabitur a mari usque ad mare & a flumine usque ad terminos orbis terrarum. Sed nulla capitalior usquam, ac detestabilior blasphemia reperitur, quàm illa est in c. quoniam de immunit. in 6. vbi Papa Ecclesiam catholicam sponsam suam appellat. Nos Iustitiam nostram, inquit, & Ecclesiae SPONSAE NOSTRAE nolentes negligere &c. Obsecro, si Diabolus humana voce loqueretur, ecquam magis nefariam proferre vocem posset? Nam inter omnes constat, solius Christi esse hoc proprium, ut Vir Ecclesiae appelletur, Ecclesia ipsius sponsa: velut apud Paulum 2.Cor. 10. Adiunxi vos uni viro, ad exhibendam virginem castam Christo. Sed alias eiusdem nefarias voces audiamus, qualis illa est 1.dist.93. Papa is est, cui tota parere debet Ecclesia. Item , c.inter corporalia, de translat.prælat. quando Papa dissoluit matrimonium, videtur quòd solus Deus dissoluit: quia Papa canonicè electus est Deus in terris. Feli. in c. ego N, De iureiur. Papa gerit vicem in terris,non puri hominis,sed veri Dei. Item Papa habet cælestè arbitrium:& ideo naturam rerum immutat, substantiam vnius rei applicando alteri: & de nihilo potest aliquid facere:& sententiam quæ nulla est, facere aliquam:quia in iis quæ vult, ei est pro ratione voluntas:nec est,qui ei dicat,Cur ita facis? ipse enim potest supra ius dispensare, & de iniustitia potest facere iustitiam,corrigendo iura & mutando:& plenitudinem obtinet potestatis, quæ totidem verbis scripta exstant in gloss.c. quando Extr. de translat.Episc. Item c.si papa,dist.40. si Papa caeteras animarum in inferos detruderet, nō tamen cuiquam liceret ex illo quærere, Cur id facis ? Ecquis est de Christiana religione bene sentiens, qui in his verborum portentis non certissimum Antichristum agnoscat? de quo Paulus ita loquitur 2. Thess.2. Patefiet homo ille nefarius,filius inquam, ille perditionis,sese opponens, & efferens aduersus id quod dicitur DEVS,aut Numen: adeò, vt in templo Dei sedeat ostentans se quasi sit Deus. Quid? quod etiā profiteri ac palam prædicare ausus est, tātam esse vim tantámque sanctitate sedis suæ, vt quicunque ganeo,& quantumuis impius,periurus, sceleratus in ea consederit, confestim ex illa sola sessione sanctimoniam hauriat?cuius nefariæ blasphemiæ testimonium hoc extat in c.non nos,dist.41. Beatus Petrus peremnem[?] meritorum dotem cum hereditate innocentiæ transmisit ad posteros. quod illi concessum est per actum lucem, ad illos pertinet, quos par conuersationis splendor illuminat. Quis enim SANCTVM dubitet esse, quem apex tantæ dignitatis attollit? in quo si desint bona acquisita per meritum, sufficiunt quæ à loci prædecessore præstantur. Obsecro, Annon illam audire fabu-lam videmur, quam poetæ de tripode Pythia con-finxerunt, & alta quadam specu, unde anhelitus sic afflabatur, ut simulatq; Pythia vates in illa tripode consedisset, hausto à tergo diuinationis spiritu cō-festim oracula funderet? Strab.9. & tamen execrata illa Papæ Symmachi blasphemia paulò post in c. multi, apertissimè Chrysostomi verbis coarguitur: ex quo & aliis sexcetis Gratianici Decreti locis de illius libri stultitia exist imari potest. Sed age: nunc alia consimiliū blasphemiarū testimonia profera-mus. Papa est Deus in terris, secundū Bal. in l. vlt. C. sent. rescind. Dec. in c. 1. de const. Feli. in c. ego N. de iure-iur. Papa & Christus faciunt vnū consistoriū: ita quod excepto peccato potest Papa quasi omnia facere, quę potest Deus, & à nemine potest iudicari: secundum Abb. in c. licet, de elect. & quæ facit, facit vt Deus, non vt homo: c. inter incorp. de translat. prælat. Cardin. Parif. in conf. 63. nu. 162. vol. 4. Papa est quodda numē & quasi visibile quendā Deum præ se ferens: vt ait Ludouicus Gomes. in reg. cancel. Papa potest de iniustitia facere iustitia. c. debitus de appellat. Papa potest contra Apostolū dispensare, & contra canones Apostolorū 38. dist. c. lector. 87. dist. presbyt. Papa est supra ius. c. proposuit, de concess. præb. Factū à Papa reputari debet factū à Deo. cap. quan-to, de translat. prælat. quarum blasphemiarū partem enumerat Philip. Deci. in conf. 137. diligenter prote-qui, num. 3. vol. 1. Iason autem præter illa superiora ex eorundem Canonistarum sententia hæc recen-set: quæ tamen (vt facilè apparet) non probat. Papa est omnia, & super omnia, secundum Baldum in l. barbarius, De officio Præto. Papa supra ius, contra ius, & extra ius omnia potest: secundum Bal. in c. cum super, de caus. prop. & pos. Papa est dominus dominatium, & ius Regis regum habet in suos subditos: secundum Bald. in c. Ecclesia, vt lit. pend. Papa potest mutare quadrata rotundis: secundum Hostiens. in c. cum venif-sent, de iudic. De potentia Papæ dubitare sacrilegium est. l. sacrilegii, C. de crimi. sacrileg. Papa enim est causa causarum. vnde non est de eius potestate inquirendum, quum prima causa nulla sit causa: secundum Bald. in d. c. Ecclesia, vt lit. penden. & nemo potest dicere Papæ, Cur ita facis? secundum Specul. in tit. de leg. §. nunc ostendendum. vers. 89. & Bald. in pralud feud. Hæc ad verbum Iason in consil. 145. circa primam, num. 3. vol. 1. quæ eadem rursus, paucis prope mutatis verbis inculcat, in consil. 95. requisitus, col. pen. vol. 4. Satis multa videmur primæ impietatis Papalis argumenta proposuisse, vt iam ab illustribus Regis Galliæ consiliariis, & clarissimis Parlamentorum senatoribus intelligi possit, non sine iustissimis & grauissimis causis Papatum à multo maxima Christianitatis parte reprobatum ac repudiatum fuisse. sed tamen alia quædam insuper addemus, atque illud imprimis: Papam tantam habere tum in Purgatorio, tum in inferis potestatem, vt quantum velit animarum numerum, quæ in illis locis cruciantur, per suas indulgentias liberare, & confestim in cœlis & beatorum sedibus collocare[?] possit. vt est in Bulla Clementis vj. & apud Antoninum Florent. part. 3. tit. 22. cap. 6. Papam habere [illegible, ~3 letters]am in cœlo potestatem, vt quem velit hominem defunctum canonizare, & in Di-vorum numerum referre possit, etiam invitis E-piscopis & Cardinalibus omnibus. Hæc Troilus Maluit. in trac. de canonissanct. 3. dub. Ex quibus & aliis consimilibus licebit agnoscere, quam vera illa fuerit Eberardi[?] Salisburgensis quondam Archiepiscopi oratio annis ab hinc ducentis habita in publico Imperij Germanici conuetu, quam ex Annalium Ioh. Aventini lib. VII. proferemus, edito Ingolstadii anno 1554. Flamines illi Babylonia, inquit, soli regnare cupiunt: ferre parem non possunt. non desistent, donec omnia pedibus suis proculcarint, atque in templo Deisedeant, extollaturque super omne id quod colitur. fames opum, sitis honorum inexplebilis est. Quo plura avido concesseris, eo plura appetit. porrige digitum, & manum concupiscet. Qui servus servorum est, dominus dominorum, perinde ac si Deus foret, esse cupit. Ingentia loquitur, quasi Deus sit. Leges commutat, suas sancit. contaminat, diripit, spoliat, fraudat, occidit, perditus homo ille, quem ANTICHRISTVM vocare solent: in cuius fronte blasphemiæ nomen scriptum est, DEVS SVM: errare non possum. In templo Dei sedet, longe lateque dominatur. Hæc Eberardus, quin etiam apud eundem Aventinum eodem libro, hæc Imperatoris Friderici II. querimonia extat in epist. ad Ottonem Bauariæ Ducem, scripta: Pontifices Romani affectant dominationem atque DIVINITATEM, nempe, ut ab omnibus haud aliter, imo magis quam Deus timeantur. Nam multos Antichristos in-esse Romanensibus illis constat: nec ullos alios exitio Christianæ religioni esse. Et paulò post: Homo ille, qui dicitur PAPA, divitiis nimirum auctus, maximo Chri-stianæ pietatis detrimento omnia sibi licere more tyrannorum putat. rationem asluum nemini, QVASI SIT DEVS, reddere vult. Id quod soli Deo conuenit, vsurpat: se errare, vllaue mendacij religione astringi non posse, credi sibi impudentissime, simulque imperiose postulat. Hæc ille. Quinetiam Erasmus in Annot. Noui testam. i. ad Timot. c. i. testatur, suo tempore in Theologorum scholis disputari hæc consueuisse. An Papa possit abrogare id, quod scriptis Apostolicis decretum est, an possit aliquid statuere, quod pugnet cum doctrina Euangelica, an possit nouum articulum condere in fidei symbolo. Vtrum maiorem habeat potestatem quam Petrus, an parem. Vtrum possit præcipere Angelis: An possit vniuersum purgatorium tollere. Vtrum simplex homo sit (O detestandam blasphemiam!) an quasi Deus participet vtramque naturam cum Christo: an clementior sit, quam fuerit Christus, cùm is non legatur quenquam à purgatorii pœnis reuocasse: An solus omnium non possit errare. Sexcenta id genus disputantur magnis editis voluminibus. Idque à magnis Theologis, præsertim professione religionis insignibus. Hæc totidem verbis Erasmus, Annotat. pag. 663.
units.tr: "The Pope," he says, "on the night of the Lord's Nativity blesses a sword, which he afterwards gives to some prince, as a sign of the infinite power conferred on the Pontiff, according to that text, 'All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.' Likewise, 'He shall have dominion from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth.'" But no more capital or detestable blasphemy is found anywhere than that in c. quoniam de immunit. in 6., where the Pope calls the Catholic Church his bride: "We, unwilling to neglect our justice and our bride the Church, etc." I beg you, if the Devil could speak with a human voice, could he utter any more wicked words? For everyone agrees that it is the peculiar property of Christ alone to be called the Husband of the Church, the Church being his bride, as in Paul, 2 Cor. 10: "I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ." But let us hear other wicked utterances of the same man, such as that in 1 dist. 93: "He is the Pope, whom the whole Church ought to obey." Likewise, c. inter corporalia, de translat. prælat.: "When the Pope dissolves a marriage, it seems that God alone dissolves it, because the Pope, canonically elected, is God on earth." Felinus on c. ego N, De iureiur.: "The Pope bears the place on earth not of a mere man but of the true God." Likewise: "The Pope has a heavenly judgement, and therefore he changes the nature of things, transferring the substance of one thing to another, and can make something out of nothing, and make a sentence that is nothing into something; for in those things which he wills, his will is his reason, and there is no one who may say to him, 'Why do you so?' For he can dispense above the law, and make justice out of injustice by correcting and changing the laws, and he holds the fullness of power," which are written word for word in the gloss on c. quando Extr. de translat. Episc. Likewise, c. si papa, dist. 40.: "If the Pope should thrust the other souls down into hell, yet it would not be lawful for anyone to ask him, 'Why do you do this?'" Who among those who think rightly of the Christian religion does not recognise in these monstrous words the most certain Antichrist, of whom Paul speaks thus in 2 Thess. 2: "That man of sin will be revealed, the son of perdition, who opposes and exalts himself above all that is called God or is worshipped, so that he sits in the temple of God, showing himself as if he were God." What of the fact that he has dared even to profess and openly proclaim that the power and sanctity of his seat is so great that whoever, however vile, however impious, perjured or wicked, sits in it, at once draws holiness from that very seating? Testimony to this wicked blasphemy is found in c. non nos, dist. 41.: "Blessed Peter handed down to posterity a stock of merits together with the inheritance of innocence. What was granted to him by the act of light pertains to those whom the splendour of a like way of life illumines. For who would doubt that he is holy whom the summit of so great a dignity lifts up? In whom, if the good works acquired by merit are lacking, those which are supplied by the predecessor of the office suffice." I beg you, do we not seem to hear that fable which the poets invented about the Pythian tripod, and about the deep cave from which the breath was so blown up that as soon as the Pythian prophetess had sat upon that tripod, having drawn in the spirit of divination from behind, she at once poured out oracles? Strabo 9. And yet that accursed blasphemy of Pope Symmachus is soon after refuted most plainly by the words of Chrysostom in c. multi; from which, and from some six hundred other passages of Gratian's Decree, the folly of that book may be judged. But come, let us now bring forward other testimonies of similar blasphemies. "The Pope is God on earth, according to Baldus on l. ult. C. sent. rescind. Decius on c. 1. de const. Felinus on c. ego N. de iure-iur. The Pope and Christ make one consistory, so that, sin excepted, the Pope can do almost everything that God can do, and he can be judged by no one, according to Abbas on c. licet, de elect.; and what he does, he does as God, not as man: c. inter incorp. de translat. prælat. Cardinal Parisius, consil. 63, n. 162, vol. 4." "The Pope is a certain divinity and bears before himself a certain visible God, as Ludovicus Gomesius says on the Rule of the Chancery." "The Pope can make justice out of injustice: c. debitus de appellat." "The Pope can dispense against the Apostle and against the canons of the Apostles, 38 dist.; c. lector 87 dist.; presbyt." "The Pope is above the law: c. proposuit, de concess. præb." "What is done by the Pope ought to be regarded as done by God: cap. quanto, de translat. prælat." Philip Decius, consil. 137, diligenter proteque, n. 3, vol. 1, enumerates some part of these blasphemies. Jason, moreover, besides those mentioned above, according to the opinion of the same canonists, recounts these, which however (as is easily seen) he does not prove. "The Pope is all things and above all things, according to Baldus on l. barbarius, De officio Praetorio. The Pope can do everything above the law, against the law and outside the law: according to Baldus on c. cum super, de caus. prop. et pos. The Pope is lord of lords, and has the right of the King of kings over his subjects," according to Baldus on c. Ecclesia, ut lit. pend. "The Pope can change squares into circles," according to Hostiensis on c. cum venissent, de iudic. "To doubt the power of the Pope is sacrilege: l. sacrilegii, C. de crimin. sacrileg. For the Pope is the cause of causes; hence it is not to be inquired into his power, since the first cause has no cause:" according to Baldus on the said c. Ecclesia, ut lit. pend. "and no one can say to the Pope, 'Why do you so?'" according to the Speculator in tit. de leg. §. nunc ostendendum, vers. 89, and Baldus in praelud. feud. These words Jason repeats verbatim in consil. 145, circa primam, n. 3, vol. 1, and again, with almost the same words changed, he inculcates them in consil. 95, requisitus, col. pen., vol. 4. We seem to have set out enough of the first arguments of Papal impiety, so that it may now be understood by the illustrious counsellors of the King of France and the most distinguished senators of the Parlements that the Papacy was not without the most just and weighty causes rejected and repudiated by the far greater part of Christendom. But we shall add certain other points besides, and this above all: "The Pope has such power both in Purgatory and in hell that he may free from those places as many souls as he wishes, by his indulgences, and at once place them in heaven and in the seats of the blessed," as is in the Bull of Clement VI and in Antoninus of Florence, part 3, tit. 22, cap. 6. "The Pope has [illegible] power in heaven, so that he may canonise whatever dead man he wishes and bring him into the number of the saints, even against the wishes of all the bishops and cardinals." Thus Troilus Maluit, in tract. de canonis. sanct., 3 dub. From these and other similar things it will be possible to recognise how true was that speech of Eberhard, once Archbishop of Salzburg, delivered about two hundred years ago in the public assembly of the German Empire, which we shall quote from Johannes Aventinus's Annals, book VII, printed at Ingolstadt in 1554. "Those Babylonian priests," he says, "desire to reign alone; they cannot bear an equal. They will not cease until they have trampled all things under their feet and sit in the temple of God, and exalt themselves above everything that is worshipped. Their hunger for wealth and thirst for honours is insatiable. The more you concede to the greedy man, the more he seeks. Offer him a finger, and he will desire the hand. He who is the servant of servants wishes to be the lord of lords, just as if he were God. He speaks great things as if he were God. He changes laws, makes his own, defiles, plunders, despoils, defrauds, kills; that lost man whom they are wont to call ANTICHRIST, on whose forehead the name of blasphemy is written: I AM GOD: I cannot err. He sits in the temple of God and rules far and wide." These are Eberhard's words. Moreover, in the same book of the same Aventinus, this complaint of the Emperor Frederick II is found in a letter written to Otto, Duke of Bavaria: "The Roman Pontiffs aspire to domination and DIVINITY, namely, that they may be feared by all no differently, indeed more, than God. For it is clear that there are many Antichrists among those Romans, and that none others are more ruinous to the Christian religion." And a little after: "That man who is called POPE, surely swelled with riches, to the greatest detriment of Christian piety, thinks that all things are permitted to him in the manner of tyrants. He wishes to render an account of his actions to no one, AS THOUGH HE WERE GOD. He usurps what belongs to God alone: he claims most impudently and at the same time imperiously that he cannot err, nor be bound by any obligation of truth. Thus far he." Indeed Erasmus, in his Annotations on the New Testament, 1 Tim. c. 1, testifies that in his time such things were customarily debated in the schools of the theologians. "Whether the Pope can abrogate what has been decreed in the apostolic writings; whether he can establish anything that conflicts with Evangelical doctrine; whether he can add a new article to the creed. Whether he has greater power than Peter, or equal. Whether he can command the angels; whether he can abolish the whole of purgatory. Whether he is a simple man (O detestable blasphemy!) or, as God, shares both natures with Christ; whether he is more merciful than Christ was, since Christ is not read to have recalled anyone from the pains of purgatory; whether he alone of all men cannot err. Six hundred questions of this kind are debated in large printed volumes, and by great theologians, especially those distinguished by their profession of religion." Thus Erasmus in so many words, Annotations, p. 663.
The crime of mocking religion.

units.la: SEd hæc, dicet fortasse quispiam, verborū tantum impietas & blasphemia est. Facta igitur eiusdē Papatus impia & nefaria è multis pauca, quasi exempli causa, proferamus: vt quiuis intelligat, Papas multis ab hinc seculis, Christianā religionem irrisui ac ludibrio habuisse. Atque illud imprimis Gregorij septimi, quod Benonis Cardinalis verbis exponemus. Imperator Henricus III, inquit, solitus erat frequenter ire ad orationem, ad ecclesiam sanctæ Mariæ, quæ est in monte Auentino, Hildebrandus debrandus autem, qui postea a Papa factus Gregorius septimus appellatus est, cum per exploratores suos omnia eius opera sollicitè inquireret, locum in quo frequentius Imperator orabat, notare fecit: & quendam promissa pecunia ad hoc induxit, ut supra trabes Ecclesiæ occultè lapides magnos collocaret, & ita aptaret, ut de alto supra caput orantis demitteret, & ipsum contereret. Quod minister tanti sceleris cum festinaret implere, & lapidem magni ponderis super trabes aptare vellet, lapis pondere suo eum traxit: & fracta sub trabibus tabula, & lapis, & ille miser homo Dei iudicio in pavimentum ecclesiæ cecidit, & eodem lapide penitus contritus est. Cuius rei gestæ ordinem postquam Romani cognouerunt, pedem illius miseri funæ[?] ligauerunt, & triduo per plateas urbis ad exemplum trahi fecerunt. Imperator autem solita clementia iussit eum sepeliri. Hactenus Beno. Vnde intelligitur quàm detestabilis Papæ impietas fuerit, qui neque loci, in quo Imperator orabat, & quem Papa sacrū sibi esse profitetur, neque temporis quo idè orabat, ratione habes, sed cæco furori atque amentiæ suæ seruiens, Imperatori ac principi suo pernicie molitus est. Age porrò, & aliud impietatis testimonium ex eodem Benone proferamus. Ioannes Portuensis Episcopus, inquit, qui intimus fuerat à secretis Hildebrandi, ascedit in ambonem beati Petri, & inter multa, audite clero & populo ait, Tale quid fecit Hildebrādus, unde deberemus vivi incedi, significans de sacramento corporis domini, quod Hildebrādus, respōsa diuina contra Imperatorē quærens, iniecit igni, contradicentibus Cardinalibus qui assistebant ei. Præclara hæc sunt pietatis Papalis testimonia in Gregorio VII. Nunc aliud de Sylvestro II. proferamus ex lib. Ioannis Stellæ, Veneti, ad Patriarchā Aquileiēse Romanæ ecclesiæ tituli S. Marci presbyterū Cardinalem. Postremò, inquit Romanus Pontifex Diabolo adiuuante fuit constitutus, hac tamen lege, vt post eius obitum & in anima & in corpore totus illius esset, cuius fraudibus tātam adeptus esset dignitatem. Post hoc quaesiuit Sylue-ster à Diabolo, quamdiu in pontificatu victurus esset? Respondit, quamdiu, inquit, in Hierusalem celebrabis, vives. Postremò quarto Pontificatus sui anno, cum quadragesimali tem-pore, in Basilica sanctæ crucis in Hierusalem Romæ sa-crificaret, fato se moriturum statim cognouit. V nde pœ-nitentia ductus, errorem suum coram populo confessus est: rogauitque omnes, vt corpus suum diabolicis arti-bus seductum, membratim detruncarent, dissectúmque ac laceratum super currum imponerent, & eo loci sepe-lirent, quo sponte ab equis foret vectum. Ferunt itaque Dei nutu, (vt scelerati discant apud Deum veniā lo-cum sibi relictum esse, modo in vita pœnituerint) equos ipsos sponte ad Lateranensem ecclesiam peruenisse, ibi-demque sepultum fuisse.
units.tr: But someone may say that these are only words, and that the impiety and blasphemy lies in the language alone. Let me therefore set forth a few of the impious and wicked deeds of this same Papacy, taken from many by way of example, so that anyone may understand that for many centuries the Popes have treated the Christian religion as a laughingstock and a mockery. And first is that of Gregory VII, which I shall set out in the words of Cardinal Benno. The Emperor Henry III, he says, was in the habit of going often to pray in the church of Saint Mary on the Aventine hill. Hildebrand, who afterwards became Pope and was called Gregory VII, when he carefully inquired into all his doings through his spies, had the place where the Emperor prayed most often marked. By the promise of money he persuaded a certain man to place large stones secretly on the beams above the church, and to arrange them so that they would fall from above onto the head of the one praying and crush him. When the minister of so great a crime was hurrying to carry it out, and wished to fix a stone of great weight on the beams, the stone dragged him down with its weight. The board beneath the beams broke, and the stone and that wretched man, by the judgment of God, fell to the floor of the church and was completely crushed by the same stone. When the Romans learned how this deed had happened, they tied a rope to the foot of that wretch and had him dragged through the streets of the city as an example. But the Emperor, with his customary clemency, ordered him buried. Thus far Benno. From this it is clear how detestable the impiety of the Pope was. He paid heed neither to the place where the Emperor prayed, which the Pope himself professes to be holy, nor to the time at which he prayed; instead, serving his blind rage and madness, he plotted destruction against his Emperor and his prince. Come now, let us bring forward another testimony of impiety from the same Benno. John, bishop of Porto, who had been most intimate with Hildebrand's secrets, went up into the pulpit of Saint Peter, and among many things said to the clergy and the people: Hildebrand did such a thing that we ought to be burned alive, meaning concerning the sacrament of the Lord's body, which Hildebrand, seeking divine answers against the Emperor, threw into the fire, while the cardinals who stood by him objected. These are remarkable testimonies of papal piety in Gregory VII. Now let us bring forward something concerning Sylvester II, from the book of John Stella of Venice, addressed to the Patriarch of Aquileia, cardinal priest of the Roman church of the title of Saint Mark. Finally, he says, the Roman Pontiff was installed with the help of the Devil, on this condition: that after his death he should belong wholly, in soul and body, to him by whose deceits he had obtained so great a dignity. After this Sylvester asked the Devil how long he would live in the pontificate. He replied, as long as you celebrate in Jerusalem, you will live. Finally, in the fourth year of his pontificate, when in Lent he was offering sacrifice in the Basilica of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem at Rome, he at once knew that he would die by fate. Moved by repentance, he confessed his error before the people and asked them all to cut his body, which had been led astray by diabolical arts, into pieces, and, once it was dismembered and torn, to place it on a cart and bury it in the place where the horses would draw it of their own accord. They say that by the will of God (so that the wicked may learn that a place with God is left open to them, provided they repent in life), the horses themselves came of their own accord to the Lateran church, and that he was buried there.

units.la: Hæc Stella Venetus. Extat etiam Ioannis Gerfonis Parisiensis academiæ re-ctoris sermo quidam Paschalis, in quo scriptum reliquit, Papam Ioannem XXII. contendisse, mortem restingui, & animas impiorum non puniri ante diem iudicii, quam illius hæresim fortiter Sorbonica eiusdem Parisiensis academiæ schola damnauit, & Papam illum ad retractationem compulit. eoque nomine papa ille Diabolus incarnatus appellatur à Concilio Constantiensi: sess. 7. Ex eodem impietatis genere illud est, quod Raphaelis Volaterrani verbis proponemus ex ipsius libro Geogr. V. vbi de Papa Syxto IV. cuius hic nosler Quinctus & nomē sumpsit, & pietatem imitatur, commemorans, ita scribit: Conscio & adiuuante Pontifice Pontifice coniurati Florentiam veniut[?], & in adem[?] sanc-ta Reparata mane omnes ad missam & sacrificium convenerunt. Salviatus interim cum suis clam armatis templo discedens, in curiam, ut vexilliferum alloquatur, alio simulato negotio proficiscitur. eo tamen consilio, ut orta cæde in templo ipse præsto esset, qui curiam simul cum magistratu invaderet. Igitur dato signo, cum Eucharistia tolleretur (notetur insigne pietatis papalis testimonium: Constituto, inquit, signo cum Eucharistia tolleretur) Bandinus Julianum Medicem Laurentii fratrem confodit. Antonius, qui primas sibi partes depoposcerat, Laurentium ex altera parte aggreditur, post tergum: paululumque infra jugulum ferit. Cum ille statim ad clamorem conversus ictum vitaret, iterare vulnus volentem propere superfugit in ædis sacrarium proximum. Tum legatus Papæ (qui signum illud cædis faciendæ contulerat, dum Eucharistia tolleretur) à civibus comprehensus, & è templo in curiam ductus, ac custodiæ traditus, pro viri dignitate tractatus est. Interea Salviatus Pisanus Episcopus, qui cum vexillifero de industria sermonem protrahebat, ut finem expectaret, statim comprehensus, eodem die ad curiæ fenestras suspensus fuit. Quo nuntio Pontifex accepto, Laurentium Medicem (quem fuga salutem sibi quæsisse docuimus) sacris interdicit, quod Dei sacerdotes legatumque attigisset, bellumque Florentinis aperte decreuit. Hæc Volateranus: Ex quibus perspicuum cuivis esse potest, quanti suam Eucharistiam Papæ facere soleant, in qua tamen adoranda, circumgestanda, veneranda, & omni honoris genere afficienda, religionem omnem Christianam positam esse volunt. Sed aliud argumentum proferendum est. Nam quid certius ad demonstrandam Paparum impietate afferri potest, quàm quod omnium sermone celebratur, moris esse Romæ, quoties Papæ peregrè proficiscuntur, vt illa Eucharistia equo alicui strigoso & exili imposita (cuius ex collo tintinnabulum propèdeat)agasoni cuidam committatur, & inter lixas & calones cæteráque impedimenta, quasi aduentus Papæ prænuntia, præmittatur. Nā in libro Ceremon. Pontifical.i.section.ca.3.scriptum ita est. Post eos ducitur per familiarem sacristæ rubro indutum, & baculum in sinistra habentem equus albus, mansuetus, portans sacramentum corporis Christi, habens ad collum tintinnabulum bene tinniens. Post sacramentum equitat immediatè sacristæ: qui, vt cæteri prælati, habet equū totum coopertum bocasino, &c. Item section.12.cap.1. Ducitur post hos equus albus, phaleratus, mansuetus & pulcher, cum tintinnabulo ad collum bene sonante, qui capsulam vehit cum sacratissimo Christi corpore. Item cap.4. Ante Pontificem semper præfertur crux per subdiaconum, & post crucem portatur corpus Christi super equum album, cum campanella &c. Atque hæc quidē pompæ Papalis instituta sunt: sed instituta dunta-xat. Nam qui Romæ frequentes sunt, summo consensu & de præcursore iumento, & de eodē inter impedimenta præmitti solito attestantur. Extat liber à Iohanne Monlucio Episcopo Valentino scriptus, qui Romæ plurimas Regis Galliæ nomine legationes obiit, & de Religione ad Reginā matrem inscriptus: cuius pag.101. verba hæc sunt, ex Gallico in Latinum conuersa: Quoties Papa peregrè proficiscitur, ne nimium honorem Eucharistiæ suæ præbere videatur, non illam manibus suis gestat: sed eam triduo vel quatriduo ante suum ex urbe egressum præ-mittit, mittit,equi tergo impositam, cui comites adiungit cantores,muliones,agasones , cæteráque aulæ suæ impedimenta,hoc est calones, lixas,& curtisanas(verba illius hæc sunt)Tum Papa qui se ipsius vicarium esse prædicat, sequitur,stipatus Cardinalibus,Episcopis , & aliis eiusdem generis primatibus.Ubi ad oppidû aduentat,tum id quod appellat corpus Christi, quod aliquandiu ibi quieuit,extra oppidû obuiâ affertur:statímque nutu inter se,sine ulla voce,consalutant, simul illud iterû ante se præmittit.sed quanto cum honore? Papa sub umbone honorifico in urbe inuehitur :corpus Christi sub dio defertur.Quid opus fuerat illud Roma efferre, & in alterum oppidû deportare,cùm parœcia nulla sit,quæ hoc genere non abundet?quid necesse est illud præmittere , quarto, sexto,decimo ante Papæ aduentû die?Si eo cosilio Papa istud instituit,ut sibi obuiam ad comitandum & cohonestandum suum in urbem ingressum referatur, nullum tam tenue est oppidulum,ubi non ejusmodi corpora reperiantur.si Roma efferri oportet, quidni Papa ipse exportat,aut certè secum deportari jubet potius,quàm interimenta,sarcinaria & calones illud præ mittit? Atqui si ad pluuiam cœlitus impetrandam (ut Lutetiæ & aliis locis fieri consueuit) signum alicuius sancti sanctæue ex uno templo in alterum deportetur, moris est, ut magna pompa & celebritate hominum id fiat:ut cruces,vexilla,tædæ ardentes,& alia ornamenta præferantur. Quinetiam plerumque ii qui simulacra illa deportant corpora nudi,ac linteis tantum amicti, aut certè nudis pedibus ingrediuntur. Et Papam non pudebit præmittere id,quod credi vult esse corpus Christi,cum paruula laternula , & in capsula inclusum,equi tergo impositum, stipatum aulæ suæ fecibus[?] ? Cui verisimile fiet,eum qui se caput ecclesiæ profitetur,tantum in se fafacinus admissurum fuisse, si vere credidisset Iesu Christi corpus sub illo sacramento corporaliter fuisse? Hæc Monlucius. quibus addi etiam illud poterit, quod ex multorum Paparum auctoritate comprobatum est, & palam in Romana ipsius ecclesia receptum ex libro conformitatum beati Francisci: sol.72. Frater Franciscus dicendo missam in calice araneam invenit: quam nolens proiicere, bibit cum sanguine. po-steafricas crus, & scalpens, ubi pruritum sentiebat, ipsa aranea a crure exiuit sine lesione fratris. Item sol.67. Quidam nomine Bonelus noluit credere quod hostia consecrata esset corpus Domini: & dixit quod sua asina comederet hostias: quod audiens B. Antonius missam celebravit, & hostiam consecratam asinæ detulit, & ostendit: statim asina genu flexit, & capite inclinato reuerentiam exhibuit. quod videns Bonelus, catholicus est factus. Annon ex huius asinæ schola didicisse Papa videtur, quod superius diximus, cum ad illum Eucharistia refertur, solere illam nutu & demisso capite salutare. Sed illius asinę mentio nobis in memoriam revocat picturam, quæ Lutetiæ plurimis in templis visitur, Sacerdotis Asinæ porrigentis altera manu missalem hostiam, altera auenam: asinæ autem, ore ab auena auerso, flexis poplitibus hostiam adorantis, eique auribus micantis, naribus arridentis.
units.tr: Thus Stella of Venice. There also exists a certain Easter sermon by John Gerson, rector of the University of Paris, in which he left it written that Pope John XXII maintained that death is extinguished and that the souls of the wicked are not punished before the day of judgment. The Sorbonne school of the same University of Paris strongly condemned this heresy and compelled that Pope to retract it. For this reason the Council of Constance, in session 7, calls that pope a Devil incarnate. Of the same kind of impiety is what we shall set out in the words of Raffaele Volaterrano, from his book Geographia, where, speaking of Pope Sixtus IV, whose name and piety our Quintus has taken and imitates, he writes as follows: With the Pope's knowledge and help, the conspirators came to Florence, and in the church of Santa Reparata they all gathered in the morning for mass and sacrifice. Meanwhile Salviati, leaving the church with his men secretly armed, set off to the palace to address the standard-bearer, on the pretext of some other business. He had this plan, however, that once the slaughter had begun in the church, he himself should be at hand to attack the palace together with the magistrates. Therefore, when the signal was given, while the Eucharist was being raised (note this mark of papal piety: when the signal had been fixed, while the Eucharist was raised), Bandini stabbed Giuliano de' Medici, brother of Lorenzo. Antonio, who had demanded the leading role for himself, attacked Lorenzo from the other side, from behind, and wounded him a little below the throat. When Lorenzo, turning at once at the cry, avoided the blow, and Antonio wished to repeat the wound, he quickly escaped into the nearby sacristy. Then the Pope's legate, who had given the signal for the slaughter while the Eucharist was being raised, was seized by the citizens, led from the church to the palace, and handed over to custody, where he was treated according to his rank. Meanwhile Salviati, bishop of Pisa, who had deliberately prolonged his talk with the standard-bearer in order to wait for the end, was at once seized and hanged from the windows of the palace that same day. When the Pope received this news, he forbade Lorenzo de' Medici (whom we have shown to have sought safety in flight) from the sacraments, because he had touched the priests of God and the legate, and he openly declared war on the Florentines. Thus Volaterrano. From these things it can be plain to anyone how much the Papists are accustomed to value their Eucharist, in which, however, they want all Christian religion to lie, to be adored, carried about, venerated, and honoured with every kind of reverence. But another argument must be brought forward. For what can be offered that is more certain for showing the impiety of the Papists than what is spoken of by everyone: that it is the custom at Rome, whenever the Popes travel abroad, that the Eucharist is placed on some lean, worn-out horse with a little bell hanging from its neck, and entrusted to a certain groom, and sent ahead among the camp-followers, the carters, the baggage, as a herald of the Pope's arrival. For in the book of ceremonies of the Pontiff, part 1, section 3, chapter 3, it is written thus: After them is led, by a servant of the sacristan dressed in red and holding a staff in his left hand, a white horse, gentle, carrying the sacrament of the body of Christ, having a bell ringing well at its neck. Immediately after the sacrament rides the sacristan, who, like the other prelates, has a horse entirely covered with cloth, etc. Likewise section 12, chapter 1: After these is led a white horse, decked with trappings, gentle and beautiful, with a bell sounding well at its neck, which carries the casket with the most sacred body of Christ. Likewise chapter 4: Before the Pontiff a cross is always carried by a subdeacon, and after the cross the body of Christ is carried upon a white horse, with a little bell, etc. These are indeed the institutions of papal pomp, but only institutions. For those who are numerous at Rome bear witness, with complete agreement, both to the forerunning beast and to the baggage that is customarily sent on ahead with it. There is a book written by John Monluc, bishop of Valence, who performed many embassies at Rome in the name of the King of France, and addressed on religion to the Queen Mother. At page 101 its words, translated from French into Latin, are these: Whenever the Pope travels abroad, lest he seem to show too much honour to his Eucharist, he does not carry it in his own hands, but sends it ahead three or four days before he leaves the city, placed on the back of a horse, to which he attaches companions: singers, muleteers, grooms, and the other baggage of his court, that is, camp-followers, carters and courtesans (these are his words). Then the Pope, who declares himself the vicar of that same one, follows, surrounded by cardinals, bishops and other princes of that sort. When he arrives at a town, that which he calls the body of Christ, which has rested there for some time, is brought to meet him outside the town, and at once, by a nod, without any word, they greet one another, and he sends it again before himself. But with what honour? The Pope is carried into the city under a honorific canopy; the body of Christ is carried in the open air. Why was it necessary to bring that out from Rome and carry it to another town, when there is no parish which does not abound in such things? Why must it be sent ahead on the fourth, sixth or tenth day before the Pope's arrival? If the Pope established this with the purpose that it should be brought out to meet him, to accompany and honour his entry into the city, there is no town so small where such bodies are not found. If it must be carried out of Rome, why does the Pope not carry it out himself, or at least order it to be carried with him rather than sending it ahead with the baggage, the carters and the camp-followers? And yet, if to obtain rain from heaven (as is customary at Paris and other places) the image of some saint, male or female, is carried from one church to another, it is the custom for this to be done with great pomp and a crowd of people, so that crosses, banners, burning torches and other ornaments are carried before it. Indeed, very often those who carry those images walk barefoot, or even naked, clad only in linen. And will the Pope not be ashamed to send ahead that which he wishes to be believed to be the body of Christ, shut up in a little lantern and casket, placed on a horse's back, surrounded by the dregs of his court? Who will think it likely that he who professes himself the head of the Church would have committed so great a sacrilege, if he had truly believed the body of Jesus Christ to be bodily present under that sacrament? Thus Monluc. To these may be added also what has been confirmed by the authority of many Popes, and openly received in the Roman church itself, from the book Conformities of Blessed Francis: folio 72. Brother Francis, saying mass, found a spider in the chalice; not wishing to throw it out, he drank it with the blood, and afterwards, scratching his leg where he felt an itch, the spider came out of his leg without harm to the brother. Likewise folio 67. A certain man named Bonellus refused to believe that the consecrated host was the body of the Lord, and said that his ass would eat the hosts. Hearing this, Blessed Anthony celebrated mass, brought the consecrated host to the ass, and showed it to him; at once the ass bent its knee and, bowing its head, showed reverence. When Bonellus saw this, he became a Catholic. Does it not seem that the Pope learned from the school of this ass what we said above, that when the Eucharist is brought to him, it is his custom to greet it with a nod and a lowered head? But the mention of that ass brings back to our memory the picture which is seen in many churches at Paris: a priest's ass, holding out a consecrated host in one forefoot and an oat in the other; and the ass, with its mouth turned away from the oats, kneeling on bent knees and adoring the host, its ears pricked up and its nostrils laughing.
On the Religions Concocted

units.la: Restat tertium Papalis impietatis argumentum. Nam cum & religionis Christianæ & Dei colendi formam à Christo & ipsius Apostolis præscriptam, atque in noui testamenti libris traditam habeamus, & Deus toties eos execretur,qui commentitias religiones in ecclesiam inuehunt: tamen Papatus noua nobis religionum figmenta inuexit, adeò absurda & ridicula, ut in tanta calamitate gratiæ tamen Deo immortali agendæ sint, quòd tantam improbitatem non nisi in stolida ingenia passus est incidere. Figmeta religionū hæc fere sunt: primum innumerabiles monachorum copiæ (genera sacrilega) quorum hæc fere nomina sunt. Franciscani, quo nomine comprehenduntur Cordigeri Conuentuales, Obseruantini, Minores, Minimi, Galochiferi, Capuchini, Amadei, Clarini, Azurini, Cartusiani, Hieronymitani, Heremitæ, & postremò Fratres ignorantiæ: quos omnes ordines Papa refert ad Francisci Assisini regulam & professionem: quem in Deorum suorum numero collocauit. Secundum locum obtinent, quos idem Papa sub regula, vexillum & nomé Augustini retulit: Heremitæ conuentuales, Sampaulini, Hieronymiani secūdi generis, Lupiniani, Apostolini, Brigidiani, Redemptionales in Hispania, Fratres prædicatores, Dominicani, siue Iacobini: Præmonstratenses, Congregationis Perusinę, Battistelli Genuenses, Ambrosiani, Doucettani, Zampanenses, Lombardi, Dalmatici, Serui Hospitalarij S. Antonij. Tertium ordine obtinent Benedictini, & sub eorum regula Cluniacenses reformati, Bernardini, Humiliati, Celestini. Huc accedunt Carmelitæ, Basiliani, Maturini, Theatini, & quos omnium istius generis veteratorum vaferrimos, callidissimos & fraudulentissimos esse constat, IESVASTRI: qui non discipulos se, aut ministros, aut sectatores Iesu profitentur, sed voce blasphema & nefaria IESV DEI socios. quasi collegas & diuini muneris participes appel-lant. Horum autem monachorum ordines singuli proprias habent,& ab aliis separatas,cucullatarum togarum formas,variis coloribus distinctas: singuli proprias ac diuersas Deorum suorum colendorum,atque (vt aperte loquuntur) religionis suæ præscriptas formulas, ritus atque instituta, longè aliorù dissimilia. Eorum autem tanta multitudo est,vt in Europa nostra facile excurrere numerus putetur ad millia quingenta.cuius rei non difficilis coniectura est: nam Sabellicus Ennead.9.lib.6.scri ptum reliquit,Francifcanorum sectam vsque adeo per vniuersum orbem pullulasse, vt quadraginta prouincias obtinuerit,& sub qualibet plures custo dias conuentus (Guardianos vocant) sexaginta millia hominum excesssse : adeo vt magister vni-uersi ordinis,quem Generalem vocant, sæpius au-ditus sit Papæ expeditionem in Turcas parati pol-liceri,ex Seraphici Francisci familia triginta bella-torum millia, qui bellica munera gnauiter obire possent:nihil sacrorum cultu interpellato. Deinde commenta sunt miraculorum&doctrinarum adeo fabulosa,vt iam plerósque illorum tantæ stultitiæ non modo pigeat,verum etiam pudeat. Neque ve-risimile cuiquam hoc tempore videretur, tantam humani quondam generis vanitatem fuisse, tan-támque religionis caliginem, nisi documenta sole ipso clariora extarent. Nam apud Romanos quidem & alias profanas gentes figmenta religionum fuisse absurdissima, nemo inficiatur. sed miseri mortales per ea tempora in tetris & caliginosis tenebris,& quasi nocte illuni sine vlla sacrarum literarum luce versabatur. Verum,vbi eiusdem scripturæ pturæ sacræ libri ex illis tenebris emerserunt, ubi Christus tanquam solis iubar generi hominum illuxit: cui verisimile videretur, Sathanam & Papas tantum per emissarios suos potuisse, ut in tanta luce tamen hominum oculos quasi fasciis præstringerent? Age igitur, & aliquot istius generis figmen-torum exempla ex Franciscanorum & Dominicanorum monumentis depromamus. Nam cum hic Papa Sixtus ex illa Franciscanorū colluuione pro-dierit, videndum est, cuiusmodi religionis forma ex illa schola nobis attulerit. Primo igitur loco prodeat peruulgatum illud oraculum, quod ex li-bro Conformitatum Franciscanarum passim in ec-clesia R. receptum atque approbatum esse docebimus. Franciscum Petri Bernardonis filium, in ec-stasi cum Christo commissum, atque compositum totidem plagis ac stigmatibus, iisdemque in locis a Christo compunctum fuisse, quot Christus in cruce pendens affectus fuerat: ob eamque causam eum appellari JESVM TYPICVM: hoc est, quasi Jesu crucifixi antitypum: ut quemadmodum character in cera signum imprimit, ita Christus sua in Francisci corpore vulnera impresserit: quemadmodum Jesus Christus est imago Patris, ita Franciscus sit imago Christi: deniq; ut Christus in Francisci corpore tanquam imago in speculo appareat. Unde illud in eiusdem libri fronte nefarium atque abominandum carmen:
units.tr: There remains the third argument of Papal impiety. We have the form of the Christian religion and the worship of God prescribed by Christ and his Apostles and handed down in the books of the New Testament. God curses over and over those who bring fictitious religions into the Church. Yet the Papacy has brought in new inventions of religion for us, so absurd and ridiculous that, in such a calamity, thanks must still be given to the immortal God, because such great wickedness has been permitted to fall only upon stupid minds. The inventions of religion are mostly these. First, there are innumerable multitudes of monks (a sacrilegious race), whose names are mostly these: Franciscans, under which name are comprised the Conventual Cordeliers, the Observants, the Minorites, the Minims, the Galochiers, the Capuchins, the Amadeans, the Clarists, the Azurines, the Carthusians, the Hieronymites, the Hermits, and last of all the Brothers of Ignorance. The Pope refers all these orders to the rule and profession of Francis of Assisi, whom he has placed among the number of his gods. In second place are those whom the same Pope has referred to the rule, banner and name of Augustine: the Conventual Hermits, the Sampaulines, the Hieronymites of the second kind, the Lupinians, the Apostolines, the Brigittines, the Redemptionists in Spain, the Friars Preachers, the Dominicans or Jacobins, the Premonstratensians, the Congregation of Perugia, the Battistelli of Genoa, the Ambrosians, the Doucettans, the Zampanese, the Lombards, the Dalmatians, and the Servants of the Hospital of St Anthony. In third place are the Benedictines, and under their rule the reformed Cluniacs, the Bernardines, the Humiliati and the Celestines. To these are added the Carmelites, the Basilians, the Maturines, the Theatines, and those who are known to be the most crafty, cunning and fraudulent of all this sort of cheats, the IESVASTRI. These do not profess themselves disciples, ministers or followers of Jesus, but with a blasphemous and wicked voice call themselves the companions of JESUS GOD, as colleagues and partners in the divine office. Now each of these orders of monks has its own cowled gowns, distinguished by various colours and separate from the others. Each has its own peculiar forms of worship of its gods, and (as they openly say) rites and institutions prescribed by its religion, very unlike those of the others. Their number is so great that in our Europe alone it is thought easily to reach five hundred thousand. The matter is not hard to conjecture: for Sabellicus has left it written (Ennead 9, book 6) that the sect of the Franciscans had so sprouted through the whole world that it held forty provinces, and under each province several custodies of convents (they call them Guardians), and that there were more than sixty thousand men. So much so that the master of the whole order, whom they call the General, was often heard promising the Pope an expedition against the Turks, with thirty thousand fighting men from the family of the Seraphic Francis, who could ably perform military service, without the worship of sacred things being interrupted. Next, they have invented miracles and doctrines so fabulous that many of them now are not only ashamed of such great folly but even embarrassed by it. Nor would it seem credible to anyone in this age that the human race once had such great vanity, and such a darkness of religion, were it not that the proofs stand out clearer than the sun itself. For no one denies that among the Romans and other profane nations the inventions of religion were most absurd. But wretched mortals in those times lived in dark and gloomy shadows, as if in a night without any light of the sacred letters. But when the books of Scripture itself emerged from those shadows, when Christ shone upon the human race like the splendour of the sun, who would think it likely that Satan and the Popes could, through their emissaries alone, dazzle the eyes of men, as with bandages, in so great a light? Come then, let us bring forth some examples of this kind of fiction from the records of the Franciscans and Dominicans. For since this Pope Sixtus has come forth from that Franciscan sewer, we must see what form of religion he has brought us from that school. First, then, let there be produced the widely known oracle, which we will show to have been received and approved everywhere in the Roman Church, from the book of the Franciscan Conformities: that Francis, son of Pietro Bernardone, was taken up into ecstasy with Christ and was marked with as many wounds and stigmata, and pierced in the same places, as Christ had been affected with while hanging on the cross; and for that reason he is called JESUS THE TYPE, that is, as it were, the antitype of Jesus crucified; so that just as a seal-mark impresses its sign in wax, so Christ impressed his wounds on the body of Francis; and just as Jesus Christ is the image of the Father, so Francis is the image of Christ; and finally, that Christ appears in the body of Francis as an image appears in a mirror. Hence that wicked and abominable verse on the title page of the same book:

units.la: Francisce, JESV TYPICE, dux normáque Minorum, Sedes nobis perpetuè da regni cœlorum.
units.tr: Francis, the type of Jesus, leader and rule of the Minorites, grant us a perpetual seat in the kingdom of heaven.

units.la: Jam vero ut quivis intelligat, cuiusmodi stigma-tisatio illa fuerit, quam ecclesia Romana credi ab omnibus fidelibus statuit, operæpretium est, verba ipsa Scriptoris attendere: siue potius monachi nostri Papæ Sixti, qui publicam illi scriptori fidem atque auctoritatem adiungi oportere statuit. Nam Non solum, inquit, manus & pedes fuerunt perforati, sed conclauati, ita quod clauui in eis apparuerunt. deinde clauorum capita erant nigra: cum tamen carni vel neruis similes esse deberent, ex quibus facti erat: tertio, capita clauorum erant oblonga & repercussa, cum tamen martellus nec ictus affuerit. quarto, in loco offoso & non molli stigmata sunt impressa. quinto, licet clauui essent carnei, vel nerui, ad instar tamen ferri erant duri, fortes & solidi. Sexto, ipsi clauui non erant breues, solum acumina habentes, seu capita: sed erant longi ad partem aliam resultantes. Septimo, clauui non stabant ex parte alia longi, sed recuruati, sic vt digitus intra recuruationem arcualem ipsorum immitti valeret. Octauo, cum clauui essent facti ex carne, vel neruis, & ex utraque parte pedum & manuum resultarent, & excederent, profecto non erant nec pedes, nec manus deformatæ, vel contractæ. Nono, clauui erant circumquaque a carne alia separati, vt pecia circumcirca ponerentur, propter sanguinis restrictionem. Decimo, clauui mouebantur, & tamen a manibus nec a pedibus remoueri poterant, cum B. Clara & alii hoc facere attentassent. Vndecimo, cicatrices clauorum & lateris per tantum tempus non sunt putrefactæ, scilicet per duos annos & ultra. Duodecimo, vulnus laterale erat ad instar vulneris Christi. insuper miraculu erat, quomodo B. Francisco, cum maximum haberet dolorem ex apertione corporis in quinque locis, videlicet manibus, pedibus, & latere, & sanguis iugiter a locis prædictis emanaret, potuerit per tantum tempus viuere, scilicet post biennium quod superuixit a stigmatum susceptione. Audisne hæc, Monache Bardocu-culle noster, qui cum per tot annos Franciscanici ordinis Antistes generalis, & magister summus fabulas istas in tuis scholis tradideris, nunc eiusdem ordinis columen, & universae (ut ais) Ecclesiae Pastor factus, eadem haec portenta nobis pro divinis oraculis tradere conaris? Quid?an si quid in te aut Franciscanis tuis pudoris aut verecundiae residueret, manerétne Blaesis, nobili Galliae civitate, nefa-rium illud de Francisco Bernardone palam pro te-pli foribus inscriptum elogium : QUAERETUR PECCATUM ILLIUS:ET NON INVENIETUR? Sed iuvat nos, unde istis oraculis auctoritatem asciscat, paulisper exponere. Nam paucis post versibus ita loquitur:Diabolus dixit, quod Christus videns Franciscum sibi datum pro signifero tanti ordinis, ipsi suorum vulnerum stigmata impressit, & clavos in manibus & pedibus, & in latere dextro, vulnus. Hac Diabolus, & quare sit factum, Diabolus adiuratus a quodam sacerdote de veritate dicenda, post plura, per os mulieris apud Rauennam morantis, nomine Zantese, sic inquit: In coelo sunt tantum duo signati, scilicet Christus & stomachosus Fracifcus. Sciens igitur Christus se daturū illi stomachoso bullam suorum stigmatum, nō permisit illi accipere a Papa bullam, manu hominis fabricatam. Haec diabolus. Verba haec sunt totidem literis exscripta ex eodem Conformitatum lib.sol.230[?].col.4.& sol.231.col.1. Ex quibus intelligi licet, quantum auctoritatis istis oraculis & huic praeclaro illorum testimonio a Sathana prolato debeatur :cùm neque Christus, neque Apostoli ferre potuerint, ut ullum sibi testimonium praeberet. Nunc generosi & illu-stres Regis Galliarum consiliarij pro sua prudentia deliberent,cùm Sixtus quartus, & Sixtus quintus ambo Franciscani,& Franciscanorum antistites,& alij Papæ complures commentitias istas, & blasphemas fabulas in Ecclesiam invexerint,ac tandiu sua auctoritate confirmarint, hodieque tantopere confirment, utrum iure an iniuria sint à maxima Christiani orbis parte sceleris atque impietatis danati. De quo ut commodius deliberare possint,alterum item locum ex eod.libr.foli. 231. subiungemus,ubi scriptum ita est: Franciscus in monte sacro Aluerniæ corporaliter eleuatus est, ut frater Leo socius eum vidit. Aliquando enim invenit eum in aëre, per tantum spatium eleuatum, quòd vix poterat tangere pedes eius,& tunc ipsos amplexabatur cum lachrymis. Aliquando invenit eum usque ad medios fagos eleuatum à terra. Aliquando invenit eum in tanta altitudine eleuatum, quòd vix eum videre poterat. Et sæpe invenit eum frater Leo cum Christo loquentem.O bone Iesu! quis est, cùm ista portenta verborum audit, qui non toto corpore perhorrescat? Nam quid aliud est populo ista pro cocione tradere, quàm Franciscum Deum corporatum facere, eúmque remoto Christo adorandum Christiano populo proponere? Et tamen tetriora etiam ac turpiora sequuntur. Nam sol.232. Franciscus ipse his loquens verbis inducitur. Post hæc D.Iesus crucifixus manus suas corpori meo applicavit,& primo manibus, secundo pedibus, tertio stigma lateris cum vehementissimo dolore sensi: & cum magna voce clamoris mei qualibet vice impressit, & verba quædam secreta mihi dixit, quæ nulli adhuc homini revelavi.Ecquem hoc seculo tam excordem futurum Cucullifer Sixtus noster putat, ut istis blasphemis ac nefarijs fabulis fidem habeat? usque eóne consiliarios Regis Galliæ & Parlamentorum senatores stupistupidos ac bardos fore arbitratur, vt non impia ista commenta simul cum illorum auctore Petri Bernardonis filio execrentur? Nisi dicat fortasse quispiam, quibus in claustris & carceribus monachorum haec nata sunt, in ijs eadem haec arcano concludi, & quasi mysteria Cereris coerceri: neque quemquam esse hodie tam expertem ingenij, qui non has norit esse fabulas aniles, & delirantium somnia. Verum, ex aduerso ecce nobis in manibus decreta Paparum horrifica, quibus seuerissimè interdicunt, ne quis de historiarum istarum fide dubitare audeat: sanciúntque vt in Ecclesia catholica Romana pro sacris oraculis recipiátur: si quis secus senserit, tum is pro haeretico & schismatico habeatur. Nam eiusdem libri sol.234.col.3. scriptum ita est:Papa Gregorius IX. de sanctitate B. Francisci, & de eius stigmatibus plures bullas fecit, in quibus asserit B. Franciscum stigmata D. Iesu veraciter in suo corpore impressa a Christo habuisse: ET HOC TENENDVM MANDAT FIDELIBVS, & credendum, & sub nota haeresis puniendum, oppositum sapienti: Dominus Alexander IV, qui stigmata vidit propriis oculis B. Francisci, ipso B. Francisco adhuc viuente, qui in bulla sic loquitur: Stigmata in eiusdem sancti corpore, dum adhuc vitali spiritu foueretur, viderunt oculi fideliter intuentes, & certissimi contrectantium digiti palpauerunt. Tertio D. Papa Nicolaus III. dedit similem bullam, quarto D. Papa Benedictus XII. Et cum S. Romana Ecclesia determinatio sit verissima, & certissima (ipsa enim Romana Ecclesia tanquam magistra sequenda est in omnibus, dist.11. in fi. dist.12[?].c.1. & seq. & dist.22.c. reputatur, dist.22.c. omnes, in fine. & qui contra eam loquitur, haereticus reputatur. dist.22.c. omnes. quod ipsa nunquam à tramite Apostolicæ traditionis errauit.24.q.1.ad quam in dubiis & arduis est recurrendum.dist. 11.c. palam.dist.12.præceptis.24.q.1.c.quoties.ipsáque valet omnes iudicare, de ipsa iudicare nulli permittitur.11.q.3. episcopo.§.Sola.17.q.4.nemini.)& ipsa Ecclesia Romana declarauit B.Franciscum stigmatisatum a Christo, ut patet ex bullis præfatis. Quare hoc est firmissime, tanquam verum, tenendum, & oppositum tenentem ut HAERETICUM ab omnibus despiciendum: & præsertim cum dicti duo summi Pontifices Gregorius & Alexander non solum oculis propriis viderint, sed fide dignis testibus hoc esse attestatum dicant expresse. Et mox col.3. Sexto, B. Francisci stigmatizatio authenticatur etiam testimonio malignorum spirituum, de quibus supra dictum est. Hactenus ex libro Conformi-tatum,sol.uti dixi.234,ut iam perspicuum omnibus esse possit, non de nihilo esse, quod tantopere hæc apud Galliæ Regis consiliarios & Parlamen-torum senatores urgemus. Neque enim pro leui-bus nugis & ludicris poetarum narrationibus hæc haberi Monachus noster Regum & Principum ex-communicator patietur: præsertim cum in Franciscanorum cœno tandiu volutatus, nunc illius se ordinis patronum ac defensorem summum profite-tur: & eos pro hæreticis haberi iubet, qui ecclesiæ Rom.non usquequaque fidem atque auctoritatem adiungent. Qua de re ne cui dubium esse possit, nō uno hæc illius libri loco traduntur, hoc est, folio 234. verum etiam in ipso lib.exordio sol.3. his verbis In quo sancto, prodigiosa stigmatizatio facta est? Certè in nullo alio, nisi in beato patre nostro Francisco: ut asserit ECCLESIA ROMANA, & fidelibus ingerit ad credendum. Deinde etiam Papa Benedictus festum de stigmastigmatibus colendum concessit ordini. Quinetiam Antoninus Episcopus Florentinus, lib. Historial. 3. tit. 24. §. 10. ita loquitur: Papa Alexander IV. anno CIↃ-CCLIIII. montem Aluernia propter impressionem sacrorum stigmatum ibi factam in corpore S. Francisci in specialem protectionem assumens immediatè, Romanæ ecclesiæ ipsum subiciens, B. Franciscum multis laudibus extollendo, montem illum sacrum à fratribus nunquam relinqui præcepto efficaci mandauit. Eodem anno Anagniæ existens misit vnum seruum Christi fidelibus literas deferentem, iuxta seriem literarum Gregorii ix. de sacris stigmatibus B. Francisci, in quibus innuit se illa propriis oculis vidisse. Item alias literas misit Archiepiscopo Genuensi, præcipiendo vt illos qui de imagine S. Francisci in Ecclesia S. Mariæ, & ministerio S. Xristi malitiosè deleuerant stigmata, citaret personaliter coram ipso, pro meritis recepturos vltionem, inhibendo sub interminatione anathematis, ne quis de cetero similia attentaret. Nicolaus tertius Papa circa annum CIↃ. CCLXXX. misit literas vniuersis Christi fidelibus, de sacris Francisci stigmatibus certum testimonium continentes.
